title: Cleaving to the Lord
english: The mind is the true vine and the true drinking of wisdom. For having been called to partake of the table prepared by wisdom, having slaughtered her own victims and having mixed her own wine, the mind, being filled with the desire of the divine banquet and expecting to be filled, says: 'Oh that my soul might be filled with satiety and drinkability' (Ps 63:5). And since, always partaking of this liturgy, it hungers because the desire of the mind is insatiable, it says 'Oh that it might be filled' and yet 'my soul has not been filled,' even though it has abundantly partaken of the food and the drink.

Let those who, after the resurrection, dream of sensible food and drink be put to shame. For it is not the flesh or the body, but the soul that is to be filled with satiety and drinkability, the desire of the soul being filled with God in good things, as it is said in another psalm. And having been filled with gladness, it rejoices gratefully toward the one who has desired the food, saying: 'And lips of gladness shall praise your name' (Ps 63:11), concerning which it is said: 'My lips shall praise you' (Ps 36:13). And virtue is the lips of gladness. For as it is said, 'members of folly,' as in the [psalm of] folly, 'the feet of those who use it bring them down' (Ps 140:12), so let not the lips also be of gladness, unless indeed in this also someone having outward things shows them through the eyes, as it was said concerning the fool, that those using them have feet bringing them down to the mire; and concerning the one rejoicing, as lips of gladness praising the approach of God.

He who avoids idleness is able to say these things, so that caring for the things of the Lord may please Him, and he who keeps his bed undefiled may honorably lie with his bride according to the holy men. Just as for the one running toward virtue and piety to reach the goal, it is said: 'I have finished the race' (2 Tim 4:7), and 'I have run without law and have directed [my course]' (Gal 5:4) (for the one who finished is the one who ran the race), so does the one following God, according to Jeremiah: 'But I have not been weary in following behind you' (Jer 2:12), and according to Hosea: 'I will go after the Lord' (Hos 2:23), and as Moses says: 'You shall go after the Lord your God' (Deut 31:8); let him finish at last the journey after God, having reached the goal of blessedness.

The end is that he will hear towards God, 'And you stand with me.' For a voice is not something of a traveler. Regarding this state, having arrived after traveling behind, as if to be joined behind, he says, 'My soul has cleaved behind you,' (Ps 63:8) signifying the voice of 'It has cleaved' [is] 'It has been united.' For it is not to be heard that those shunning the evil are being joined to the good. He shows [union] towards God, and 'He who is joined to the Lord is in the spirit.' It is not to be sought whether it is the same thing, 'My soul has cleaved behind you,' so as not to corrupt the joining to the Lord and the joining of the soul behind another, desiring the end to be the same joining to the Lord. For the end of traveling behind the Lord is the joining of the soul of the one traveling behind him; however, even if reaching [union] behind is also an end of a journey, there is nothing more perfect than the joining to the Lord in the spirit to become with him.

As he receives the things of the vision, he confesses that his soul has been cleaved behind God, grasping the right hand of God. And this is the only-begotten power of God; grasping and holding securely, the nearby visible and invisible enemies sought in vain the soul of him saying these things, unable to snatch away the one being guarded by the mighty hand of God (Ps 62:10b,11). 'Let the sinners be turned away into Sheol, all the Gentiles who forget God' (Ps 58:5) is in agreement with the entering of the wicked into the lowest parts of the earth. And having entered, they shall be delivered to punishment, the sword being signified by the name. The hands of this sword, or rather, it works pains and bitterness to those serving it, being called vessels of wrath in others. And it calls the evil powers a 'fox-catcher,' because of the cunning, deceitful, and malicious [nature] of those called fox-catchers.

And the present things are to be interpreted otherwise: since it is commanded to become material and fleshly such a one, you will say he has sunk himself down to the earth as if to have entered into its lowest parts by choice. And those who are delivered to dishonorable sufferings undergo this, having desired it with the desires of their hearts toward impurity. By this...

title: The Triumph of Truth over Deception
english: In the same manner, both Pharaoh and those around him were swallowed up under the earth, and Moses, as in a triumphal hymn [Ps 118:12b: 'Stretch out your right hand, O God'], says the earth swallowed them. And indeed, in the historical sense, they were not swallowed under the earth, but under the depths; those having been swallowed thus under the earth and having descended into the lowest parts of the earth, they were delivered into the hands of the devil's swords, allegorically so-called. And his hands are either his angels or his skillful actions. They, having been delivered thus, shall become portions of foxes.

[Ps 62:12b: 'And the one swearing by God shall be praised, who rejoices the king.'] [Ps 63:2b: 'God works fear, not necessarily overturning or casting down the opponent, but granting courage to the one praying.'] [Ps 63:3, 4a: 'Regarding the double harm of evil, both in thought and in deed, there are two phalanxes attacking the righteous, from whom the one praying asks God to be saved unharmed from the things set before him, saying, "Protect me from the distortion of the truth of the dogmas" (for they are those wishing to corrupt the truth of the dogmas), but also from those performing practical injustice and wishing to drag me into it. For both these camps have sharpened their tongues like swords, as if having a word, the ones committing adultery gathering together with a pseudonymous knowledge, and the others with practical wickedness.'] [Ps 63:6ab: 'Moreover, even if they are not prepared wickedly, the benefactor God gives signs to those fearing him to flee from the face of the bow.'] It is said that finding a bitter thing (and such is every evil and impious dogma), they, having aimed this, shoot the bow from it, having an analogy of arrows to the burning arrows of the enemy.]

[Ps 63:6c: 'And the heterodox say that no one is able to grasp their embellished and sophistically-made teaching.'] [Ps 63:7, 8a: 'When [the wicked] are failing, you will search; you will search out because they have searched out lawlessness very much, so as to strengthen an evil word for themselves and to hide snares in their narratives, which they have striven to produce with much elegance and take pride in as if they were unassailable words, so that no one may see them.']

To expose the deception, a true man comes to them, preserving the image and the being, being a learned person with a deep heart—that is, possessing deep understanding—as one who exalts God by seizing the wise in their craftiness. Likewise, through the Apostle Paul, He revealed the guile and craftiness of Elymas the sorcerer (Acts 13:6-12). For how will not God be exalted through holy men, as the error of the deceivers is being loosed? The pharmacists and flatterers of Egypt thought much of sorcery and sophistry, but Moses, the theophany of God, possessing in himself a deep heart, having approached, overturned the deception upon which they thought much. And thus God was exalted, being remembered by all.

And he who possesses this deep understanding receives it from the Spirit who searches all things. Just as the arrows sent of the prudent do not strike even to a speck, wounding anything (Ps 63:8b–10), so also the capture has left a bitter thing upon the prepared sophists, their matter being overturned; and their tongues grew weak, that is, their words, as if they were unable to strike even in quantity the door of faith being taken up. The men, observing the things foretold, having formerly testified to their own skill, were troubled, no longer remaining in the false opinions of the sophists, having received fear because of being associated with such impious doctrines.

For having learned from them that providence is not, that all things are carried by necessity, and having been snatched away along with other deceivers, they received both naturally good and bad men, and added that fate is presiding. These false opinions being shaken, they were troubled, and they revealed the truth: that God is the maker of all things and the provider. For they reported the works of providence and understood His creatures, and they came to know the one who provides, having observed the Creator in proportion to their greatness and beauty.

When the error is being reproved, the righteous man will rejoice in God (Ps 63:11), seeing the men who formerly wandered now announcing the works of God and having understanding of His works. And because of this, he will much more hope in the Lord in whom...

title: The Election and the Temple of God
english: She rejoiced, as it remains to praise only those having a straight heart in practical and contemplative life. Regarding Psalm 64 (Ps 64:1), it was said previously that the psalm denotes practice, while the hymn denotes contemplation. The practical life, being perfected by the contemplative life, demonstrates a perfect man.

From the spoken [word] one must move toward the ecclesiastical opinion. Because of the aim of the truth, being called Zion, in this appropriately hymn and prayer is given to the Cause of all things. The hymn signifies the contemplation of God and of the truth, and the prayer signifies thanksgiving. Therefore, let him who is giving thanks in everything in Zion do this, beginning from the hymn; the prayer gives its due.

Therefore, we approach with mind and spirit to God, listening to prayer, O Lord; and we have not deserved that the lion should have power over those whom we have been honored to be impious through ignorance. All flesh comes to God, the Gentiles having the power to come from the ends of the earth toward you, and all the Gentiles whom you made are before you (Ps 64:3b). It is also to be understood that all flesh comes to God, the well-disposed soul being struck toward the easiest path by the divine laws and the characters of the truth; as it is signified, it has been said that the spiritual law is written on the tablets of the heart, not on tablets of stone. This is also presented from the prophecy of Ezekiel, God saying concerning the hard-hearted, spoken in foolishness: I will remove from them the stony hearts and I will put in them hearts of flesh, so that they may walk according to my commands (Ezekiel 36:26).

The one chosen through holiness, if he remains in the election, is received by God, as having been relocated by him from the place of the earth to dwell in the courts of the chosen one, concerning whom it has been said: Enter into his courts with hymns; and one having desire from there places it upon him, and my soul is enclosed in the courts of the Lord (Ps 64:5ab). And since the end of blessedness is not in the courts, he who is received there dwells, so as to progress and having come to the home, he may dwell being blessed; for he says, Blessed are those who dwell in your house, they shall praise you forever and ever (Ps 84:4).

What is more perfect than to be chosen and then to be received by the one who chose? It is evident from: 'In your counsel you guided me and received me with glory' (Ps 64:5). For the one chosen does all things according to the will of God, and then receives the promises with glory. These words are brought forth by those who, having been delivered from life, give glory.

Paul, sending the church of God to Timothy, calls it: 'If you delay, see how you ought to conduct yourself in the household of God, which is the living church of God' (1 Tim 3:15). From this household come the good gifts of the Spirit, as well as the things concerning the Trinity and the rest of the doctrines, which are the statutes and canons handed down by the apostles. Those who have said, 'We have glorified [Him], who said, Let atonement be made for our ungodliness, those strengthened by words against us,' expect to be filled with these good things.

Virtue, signified by the name of righteousness, is marvelously fulfilled in Him. The one believing and working good things, having been filled, has the Lord within himself; for it is said through faith that Christ dwells in the inner man. Thus the Lord, coming to the one keeping His word, makes a dwelling for Himself, so that the man is a holy temple; for it is written, 'Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?' (1 Cor 3:16) and also, 'For the temple of God is holy, and you are [that temple]' (1 Cor 3:17). It is also marvelous, and he is made upright in righteousness through the standing of Jesus Christ, full of the good divine gifts of the Spirit, of which those expecting to share say, 'We shall be filled.'

For how could those dwelling at the borders not have been afraid and the Gentiles been stirred, when the charms were abolished, so that the prophetic demons could no longer boast, and with these magic and drugs were being abolished, and he, Satan himself, having the power of death, was being rendered powerless? For the signs that were accomplished were sufficient, showing that God exists.
